claims.text: An adaptive hierarchical free-energy integration scheme using machine-learned surrogates can accurately reproduce the free-energy landscape near fusion.
The proposed scheme can retain vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration contributions to free energy.
The proposed scheme can describe both solid and fluid phases.
The proposed scheme will cost substantially less than full ab initio molecular dynamics.
The proposed scheme will be faster than TOR-TILD for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The workflow will strategically sample a sparse subset of ab initio molecular-dynamics trajectories.
Machine-learning surrogates will be trained within an adaptive hierarchical integration framework to interpolate free energies across configurations.
Machine-learned models can encode a complex energetic and entropic landscape from selected ab initio molecular-dynamics snapshots.
Adaptive selection of informative solid and fluid configurations permits interpolation of all relevant free-energy contributions across phase space.
Reducing the number of ab initio molecular-dynamics calculations will reduce computational cost.
Sparse adaptive sampling can reduce ab initio calculations without materially degrading phase-free-energy fidelity.
The resulting free-energy curves and melting temperatures will closely match full ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
The method may achieve a speedup of one to two orders of magnitude over explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The method will provide a significant performance improvement over TOR-TILD in multicomponent systems.
Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics free-energy evaluation is accurate but computationally prohibitive for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling are critical under the targeted near-melting conditions.
The method applies to high-temperature metallic systems for which density-functional theory reliably captures interatomic interactions.
The method may not extend to strongly electronically correlated systems or other systems where density-functional theory fails.
The speed–fidelity trade-off may depend on the complexity of the energy landscape, and inadequate adaptive sampling may miss critical configurations.
